subject: health
title: Launch and diagnostic: values, needs, and beliefs as internal influences on behavior
focus: values, needs, and beliefs as internal influences on behavior
essentialQuestion: Which influences are actually steering my health behavior, and which ones did I choose?
keyPoints: Values, needs, beliefs, knowledge, and emotions can influence behavior internally; naming an influence makes it available for reflection but does not automatically dictate the choice.
A durable plan names the goal, constraints, feasible options, support and backup routes, plus the evidence or condition that should trigger review and revision.

For values, needs, and beliefs as internal influences on behavior, a strong response distinguishes fact from assumption, uses a fictional or public case, and includes a safe next step or appropriate source of support.
privacySafeScenario: Map the influence field around a fictional learner facing a health choice, rank which influences carry the most weight, and propose one change that shifts the field rather than blaming the person.
studentTask: Build a decision organizer for a fictional person working on values, needs, and beliefs as internal influences on behavior. Record the goal, two influences or constraints, two options, the safest feasible choice, a support or backup route, and the evidence that would trigger a later revision.
knowledgeCheck: In two or three sentences, explain the most important distinction in values, needs, and beliefs as internal influences on behavior; use one lesson fact and name the evidence, safety check, or support route that makes the explanation dependable.
completionCriteria: The response completes every named part of the values, needs, and beliefs as internal influences on behavior task using the supplied fictional or public case.
